about: One GodEye design file: a new feature drawn before any code, one level at a time, in plain words. The page lays out each sheet from the grid positions and draws every line itself.

idea.name: Idea
idea.asks: Who uses it, the problem, what done looks like, and the outside systems.

flow.name: Flow
flow.asks: What the user does, step by step.

system.name: System
system.asks: Which parts do the work and what moves between them.

parts.name: Parts
parts.asks: Inside one app or service: its pieces and which piece uses which.

logic.name: Logic
logic.asks: One hard piece as a flowchart in plain words: steps, yes/no, loops.

build.name: Build
build.asks: The slices Claude builds one at a time, each checked against its sheets.

rules: Plain words only, zero code: no file, function, class, table, route or variable names. Name things the way the user would.
No em or en dashes. Never cut text with ... or a character limit.

Sheet 1 is the idea and holds exactly one feature box. Sheet 2 is the flow, sheet 3 the system, sheet 4 the build slices. A box on sheet 3 opens sheet 3.N (its parts), and a part on sheet 3.N opens sheet 3.N.M (its logic).
Every sheet 3.N and 3.N.M is opened by exactly one box on its parent sheet, through that box's opens field. The feature box on sheet 1 may open sheet 2.
A sheet holds at most 7 work boxes (apps, services, parts, steps, slices). When a sheet needs more, group some into one box that opens its own sheet.

A parts sheet keeps the connections of the box that opens it: every line that touches that box on sheet 3 shows up on the parts sheet as a port, written ^ plus the other box's id, in the same direction.
Boxes sit on a grid: at is [column, row], whole numbers from 0 up to 11, one box per cell. The page spaces the grid and draws every line.
A main line carries order, a number from 1, and the main lines on one sheet are numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on.
see and from point at other boxes as sheet/box, for example 3.2/run.
status on a sheet is draft until the user says ok to it, then approved. A slice status is next, building or built.
